source.title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials

approach: adaptive reduced basis and sampled elements
method.claim_scope: quasi-static hyperelastic constitutive identification from structural force/displacement data
method.acceptance: matched full-order comparison, held-out specimens/load paths, localization stress test, independent full-order verification, physical admissibility and complete cost boundary
falsifiers: held-out full-order error above frozen tolerance

cross_lane_edges.A_F: Inverse-model training becomes a compute workload only under matched accepted-output, failed-run and cost accounting.
cross_lane_edges.D_G: Mechanical constitutive model may inform package/fixture/process design only after material-specific validation; no chip/factory claim.
cross_lane_edges.E_F: Possible method for structural-material iteration cost; no Pangola chemistry, fuel, fusion or lifecycle-cost outcome.
cross_lane_edges.H: Preserve strategic materials and future-industry context while keeping preprint claims external.

fnd_eqn_status.FND-001: No physical work/heat or memory measurement.
fnd_eqn_status.FND-006: No new equation candidate; constrained model method only.
fnd_eqn_status.EQN-001_to_006: No UQPU equation-discovery benchmark or physical-law promotion.

invariant_disposition.INV-030: No Pangola carbon functional substitution result; future mechanical-composite use would need its own data.
invariant_disposition.INV-035: No new physical law; known constraints remain binding.
invariant_disposition.INV-025_026_027: Moonshots and open-frontier requirements remain preserved.

next_gate: Pin source/data/solver revisions and licenses; reproduce a small full-order reference; then compare hyperreduction with held-out localization and full-order checks.
